title: ShinyHunters claims to return after FBI arrests, uses old PGP keys as proof
content_md: The ShinyHunters extortion gang claims to have returned in posts on a new data leak site after a series of arrests over the past two months targeting alleged members. The new Tor site, launched on November 23, contains messages in both Russian and English announcing the group's return, distancing itself from alleged impostors, and denouncing a former member who was reportedly arrested and is cooperating with law enforcement. The site also includes two verification messages signed using historical ShinyHunters PGP keys dating back to 2020, including one previously used to authenticate communications with BleepingComputer in August 2025. BleepingComputer confirmed that both messages were signed using known PGP keys associated with the ShinyHunters extortion gang, confirming that the new operators have access to private signing keys historically used by the group. However, these keys do not confirm whether the individuals behind the new operation are the same people who previously controlled the group, as the keys have circulated among numerous people. The announcement follows a series of law enforcement operations targeting alleged ShinyHunters members after the group claimed to have breached FBI systems in September using an Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability. Later that month, Dutch police confirmed the arrest of a 24-year-old Amsterdam man suspected of involvement with ShinyHunters, who was identified in media reports as Pepijn van der Stap, previously known online as Umbreon.
